newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares sharply lower in early bourse.
newsitem.headline: German shares sharply lower in early bourse.

text.p: German shares were sharply lower in early bourse trade on Tuesday, as dealers said market nervousness at recent record levels on the DAX index was finally translating into the long-awaited correction.
The DAX-30 index was down 45.53 points, or 1.50 percent, at 2,985.15 points in early bourse trade and the March DAX future contract was down 15 points at 2,999 points.

"We started off brightly but no-one really knew why. There is a lot of nervousness about and there has been for a while, and you wouldn't want to get carried away with optimism on a day like this," said one trader.
Another trader said: "My guess is we will correct a little today -- we really are overdue for a correction."

A strong performer in both pre-bourse trade and early bourse trade was the banking sector, particularly Germany's biggest bank Deutsche Bank AG, which was up 16 pfennigs at 81.40 marks in early bourse trade, although this was way off earlier highs.
Also, Commerzbank was up 15 pfennigs at 44.80 marks, again off earlier highs.

"This is a continuing sector rotation -- everyone is looking at the banks right now and they have been in favour for a while now. Deutsche in particularly is enjoying a huge run," said one Frankfurt trader.
Shares in chemicals and metals group Degussa AG were up 2.66 percent at 734 marks after the group said pre-tax profits jumped 20 percent in the first quarter of the 1996/97 business year.

Another big gainer was the drugs and chemicals group Merck KGaA, which was up 1.50 marks, or 2.58 percent, at 59.75 marks after reporting an 11.3 percent rise in 1996 group sales and forecasting a strong profit growth for the year.
Airline Lufthansa shares were also higher, up 34 pfennigs at 22.70 marks, as dealers said the stock broke through a point of technical resistance.

Such resistance points occur for financial securities because of the balance of demand and supply in the market. Once a security has breached a resistance point, it can often go on to make large gains.
German equities took a hit after the west German business climate index from the research institute Ifo fell to 95.8 in December from 96.9.
However, dealers said that there had been rumours of a fall to 95.5 and attributed the decline more to overall market jitters than anything specifically related to the Ifo figures.
